title: Completion of an excellent henselian local domain is a domain
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative excellent henselian Noetherian local ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that $A$ is an integral domain, meaning that $1\ne0$ and a product of two nonzero elements is nonzero. Then its maximal-ideal-adic completion $\widehat A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is an integral domain.

source.place: Expose I Corollary 6.3(ii), printed p.14, final sentence; explicitly invoked at the start of the proof of III Proposition 3.1, printed p.37.

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and let $B\subseteq K$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K$. Excellence implies quasi-excellence, hence $A$ is Nagata. The zero ideal is prime because $A$ is a domain, so the Nagata definition makes $A=A/(0)$ Japanese. Apply the Japanese condition to the degree-one field extension $K/K$: $B$ is finite as an $A$-module. The integral-closure theorem also makes $B$ a normal domain, and $A\hookrightarrow B$ is the inclusion into $K$.

source.place: I Corollary 6.3(i), proof: normalization A-prime; I Proposition 6.2. Finiteness is expanded using Stacks Tag 07QV and definitions 032R, 032F; normality is Tag 034L.

proof.text:
Apply the finite-over-henselian product theorem to $A	o B$. Remove any zero factors from its finite product of henselian local rings. There is at least one remaining factor, since $B\subset K$ contains $1
e0$. There cannot be two: the idempotent equal to $1$ on one factor and $0$ on the others would have both $e
e0$ and $1-e
e0$, whereas $e(1-e)=0$ in the domain $B$. Thus $B$ itself is henselian local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: I Corollary 6.3(ii), proof: a henselian integral ring is unibranch; expand locality of its finite normalization using Stacks Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian).

proof.text: A finite set of $A$-module generators of $B$ also generates $B$ as an $A$-algebra: every element is already an $A$-linear polynomial in those generators. Hence $B$ is of finite type over $A$. The excellence permanence theorem, with the multiplicative set $\{1\}$, makes $B$ excellent. In particular $B$ is Noetherian, by the definition of excellence.

source.place: I Corollary 6.3(i), normal-completion argument; permanence under finite extension from Stacks Tag 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent).

proof.text: Now $B$ satisfies precisely the normal excellent Noetherian local domain hypotheses of the completion clause of [lem-per-henselian-normal-completion-preparation]. It follows that its maximal-ideal completion $\widehat B_{\mathfrak n}=\varprojlim_jB/\mathfrak n^j$ is a normal Noetherian local domain.

source.place: I Corollary 6.3(i), proof: the completed normalization is normal and local, hence integral; normal completion is Stacks Tag 0C23 (lemma-completion-normal-local-ring).

proof.text: Complete the exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to B/A\to0$ with respect to $\mathfrak m$. All three modules are finite: $A$ is generated by $1$, $B$ is finite by step 1, and the images of its generators generate $B/A$. Exactness of completion gives an injection $\widehat A\hookrightarrow\varprojlim_jB/\mathfrak m^jB$, given by the quotient maps induced by $A\hookrightarrow B$; it preserves multiplication and $1$ coordinatewise. Every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak m$ is maximal by the integral-prime theorem, since each element of $B$ is integral over $A$ by construction. As $B$ is local, $\mathfrak n$ is therefore the unique such prime. Apply finite-extension completion with $R=A$, $S=B$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$: its stated comparison identifies the $\mathfrak mB$-adic completion of $B$ with $\widehat B_{\mathfrak n}$. Here $A_{\mathfrak m}=A$ and $B_{\mathfrak n}=B$, because localization inverts only units. We have obtained an injective unital ring map $f:\widehat A\to\widehat B_{\mathfrak n}$.

source.place: I Corollary 6.3(i), proof, inclusion of the completion into the completed normalization; Stacks Tags 00MB (lemma-completion-flat) and 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension).

proof.text: Since the target of $f$ is a domain, $1\ne0$ in $\widehat A$: otherwise their images in $\widehat B_{\mathfrak n}$ would coincide. If $xy=0$ in $\widehat A$, then $f(x)f(y)=0$; thus $f(x)=0$ or $f(y)=0$, and injectivity gives $x=0$ or $y=0$. This is exactly the asserted integral-domain property.

source.place: I Corollary 6.3(i), final sentence of the proof, and 6.3(ii), final assertion.

proof_origin.place: Expose I Proposition 6.2 and Corollary 6.3(i)-(ii), printed p.14; the finite-normalization inclusion is expanded using Stacks 00MB and 07N9.

The delivery follows that route and has 6 steps, no new nodes and an unchanged statement. (1) Excellent ⇒ Nagata ⇒ N-2 at the zero prime with L=K, so the normalization B is a finite, normal domain. (2) By the finite-over-henselian product theorem and the domain idempotent argument, B is henselian local with n∩A=m. (3) B is of finite type over A, so it is excellent and Noetherian. (4) The completion of the normal excellent local domain B is a normal domain (Stacks 0C23 clause). (5) Exactness of completion on 0→A→B→B/A gives Â↪lim B/m^jB, and the finite-extension completion theorem identifies that ring with B̂_n because n is the unique prime over m. (6) A unital injection into a domain makes Â a domain. Edge cases checked: field, normal A, any characteristic, empty product.
